correctness.rationale: For any countable finitary algebraic signature, exhaust its equations by finite E_m. Each approximant Th((Phi∩E_m)∪(Psi∩E_m)) is continuous because it depends on finitely many clopen input bits, and every fixed output equation eventually has its true membership by finitary equational derivations. Thus join is pointwise limit of continuous maps into the space of closed theories. For one unary f, T_n=Th(f^n(x)=x) converges to the minimal theory: cross-variable identities are refuted by disjoint n-cycles; f^a(x)=f^b(x) for a!=b holds precisely when n divides a-b. With Psi=Th(f²=f), every join T_n∨Psi entails f(x)=x but Psi alone does not (nonidentity 2-point constant map). Hence join is discontinuous. Checked the divisibility and constant-map witness directly; proof is logical and not a finite computational induction.
